# Sum of balls, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_add_1_full` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, that contains $x + y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$. A ball may also be the whole line or the empty set.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x + y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X + Y` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` |  |
| `X += Y` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` |  |
| `X + a` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `a + X` | `T`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `X + c` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `c + X` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `X += a` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `X += c` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **B1.** The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball, the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- **B2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when an operand ball is empty.
- **B3.** If $Z$ is a finite ball, then $X$ and $Y$ are finite balls, and $\lvert (x + y) - c_w\rvert \le r_w$ for all real $x$ and $y$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$, $\lvert y - c_y\rvert \le r_y$.
- **B4.** If $X$ and $Y$ are finite balls and $\lvert \lvert c_x + c_y\rvert + r_x + r_y\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max} - 2}$, then $Z$ is a finite ball. The conditions are on the exact values of the operands, and $2^{e_{\max}}$ is the overflow threshold of `T`, just above its largest finite number: $2^{e_{\max} - 2}$ is $2^{1022}$ for `double`, $2^{126}$ for `float`.
- It follows that in every case $Z$ contains $x + y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$: the whole line contains every real number, and an empty operand has no points.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_add_1_full_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallFinite.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallFinite.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_add_1_full_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_add_1_full_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** ball_add_1, then the fix-up of the special states of a ball (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** core: as ball_add_1; fix-up: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_add_1_full.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_add_1_full.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_add_1`](ball_add_1.md).

```
# The sum of balls with one-limb centers, with the special states of a ball:
# ball_add_1, then the fix-up of milestone1.md, "Ball kernels".
# finite_when (statement B4): the result is a finite ball when no sum x + y of members of the
# operands exceeds a quarter of the overflow threshold in magnitude, |cx + cy| + rx + ry <= 2^(emax - 2).

(cz, rz) = ball_add_1(cx, rx, cy, ry)
q        = add(rx, ry)
e        = eq(q, q)
a        = abs(cz)
f1       = lt(a, const inf)
f2       = lt(rz, const inf)
f        = and(f1, f2)
c0       = select(f, cz, 0)
r        = select(f, rz, const inf)
cw       = select(e, c0, q)
rw       = select(e, r, q)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#ball_add_1_full)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

**The condition of this claim was not judged by every run.** The claims gained it (B4: finite operands under the condition give a finite ball) after the main runs, which judged the kernel without it, with no condition claimed; the supplementary run at commit `f7e0b6d` judged it, on the cases of its rows below.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 122 400 000 | 0 | 1 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 122 400 000 | 0 | 1 |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats | 3 420 868 | 0 | 1 (`fp:3:-4:1`) |
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled, supplementary run: 60 runners on 3 machines | 146 400 000 | 0 | 1 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled, supplementary run: 60 runners on 3 machines | 146 400 000 | 0 | 1 |
| toy formats, every operand, supplementary run: 3 domains of 3 formats | 3 420 868 | 0 | 1 (`fp:3:-4:1`) |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
